blocks: This is Mounjaro. One shot a week, and for many people, hunger gets quiet. Here is what it actually does inside your body.
When you eat, your gut releases two hormones, GLP-1 and GIP. They carry one message: food has arrived.
But your body breaks them down within minutes. Mounjaro is a single molecule that copies both, with a fatty tail that keeps it in your blood for days.
In the pancreas, it unlocks insulin, but only when blood sugar is high, and it holds back glucagon. Sugar comes down.
In the stomach, it slows the exit. Food stays longer, so you feel full sooner.
And in the brain, it reaches the appetite centers. Hunger signals get weaker.
In a large trial, people on the highest dose lost about twenty one percent of their body weight in seventy two weeks. Placebo: about three.
Nausea is common, especially at first. It is a prescription drug, so the dose is your doctor's call.
